extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Annals of Probability (researchers in probability/stochastic processes).
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Annals of Probability, including formatting, submission procedure, length expectations, affiliations, acknowledgements, and supplemental material rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission conditions (originality and approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies (a) that the same work has not been published before; (b) that it is not under consideration for publication elsewhere; and (c) that its publication has been approved by all co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure the work is original to this submission, not simultaneously submitted elsewhere, and that all co-authors have approved the submission before uploading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission procedure (EJMS, registration, PDF upload)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be submitted electronically. Authors should access the Electronic Journal Management System (EJMS) at https://www.e-publications.org/ims/submission/. First-time users must complete registration (only once) and then submit the manuscript by completing the form and uploading a PDF file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the EJMS workflow: register if necessary, complete submission form, and upload the PDF. This is a procedural requirement for all submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LaTeX and the Annals of Probability template
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be written in LaTeX using AOP’s template. Template will set proper margins and font; sample.pdf and sample.tex files assist in preparation of a camera-ready paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided template and sample files to achieve correct structure and layout. Do not use any packages or commands that affect the layout or formatting of your document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter layout/formatting (no packages/commands that affect layout)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not use any packages or commands that affect the layout or formatting of your document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid custom styling, macros, or package options that change margins, fonts, spacing, or other layout properties—use the template as-is to ensure consistent journal appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length expectation and handling of long papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal space is extremely valuable. If your manuscript exceeds 60 pages using the standard style files from the Annals of Probability, consider optimizing your presentation or placing part of the work as Supplementary Material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to seriously work on presentation and submit only when optimal. Acceptance of a long paper may require placing part of it as Supplementary Material; such papers may alternatively face much longer publication delay. If near/over 60 pages, proactively shorten or move material to supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The acceptance of a long paper may require that the authors place part of it as Supplementary Material. If your paper has supplemental material please follow the instructions (linked on the site).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Annals of Probability Supplement Instructions for the required format, submission process, and what material is appropriate for supplement versus the main paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliations and addresses format
rubrics_metrics.description: Please list one affiliation per author (department and university only). If an author has more than one affiliation, the others should be listed in the Acknowledgments section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single, concise affiliation (department + university) for each author on the author list; place secondary affiliations in acknowledgements rather than in the formal author-affiliation block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements: permissible content
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements should be limited to referencing: (a) named individuals who have contributed to the research by providing tangible inputs such as ideas, feedback, or code, (b) possibly-anonymous individuals who have served in the paper’s evaluation via the refereeing and editorial process, (c) organizations that provided funding, and/or (d) scientific institutions or meetings where the research was conducted or facilitated, if other than the home institution of an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep acknowledgements focused and limited to tangible contributions, evaluation assistance, funding sources, and relevant external institutions or meetings. Avoid including non-substantive or promotional acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation quality expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal space is extremely valuable. The authors are advised to seriously work on the presentation of the manuscript and submit it only when they believe it to be optimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clear exposition, concise presentation, and polished typesetting before submission to improve chances of acceptance and reduce need for editorial trimming.
